claimDiscipline.precedent: DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001 amendment A3 records FABLE-R16 doing exactly this — refusing all six assigned families at the claim gate because none was granted, then doing read-only work and raising the finding rather than deciding it. I followed that pattern.

legalStandardRead: DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001 read in full including A1 (ask the repository first; a named checkable authority stands in only where the record is empty), A2 (the repository is every committed record the family binds plus every record the route census names as a requiredSourceId), A3 (holding is per FACT, not per document; a record answers only the route it addresses), and A4 (the ask-first test extends to REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING, FILING_DESTINATION and SERVICE where the failure is withholding or denying something the repository establishes, and a packet may never tell a participant it does not state something it does state). No fee, service or destination sentence was written to any participant, because nothing was built.

families.reassignmentReason: RCW 13.50.260 is exactly the statute the brief was right to be careful about — it is largely automatic. It has both an immediate mandatory seal on acquittal or dismissal with prejudice and a court-scheduled administrative sealing hearing. The census has BOTH already, as separate keys: acquittal_or_dismissal_immediate_automatic and scheduled_administrative_hearing_automatic, each processActor=court, participantCanInitiate=false, currentOutputStrategy=process_guidance. Neither is mine. Mine is the residual branch for people the automatic process does not reach or has denied, and for them the statute requires a motion.

checkoutPosture.verdict: Packet checkout is disabled for all nine routes, and I changed nothing that bears on it.
checkoutPosture.howEstablished: data/rcap-ledger/packet-fulfillment-records.json holds exactly one fulfillment record and none of the nine routes appears in it. src/lib/expungement-ai/packet-fulfillment-authority.ts is fail-closed by design: 'commercial authority is granted only by an exact Grade-A fulfillment record, and the absence of a record is a refusal rather than a gap.' Checkout creation, consumer payment authority, sponsored entitlement and packet-credit consumption all pass through assertPacketFulfillmentProven.
checkoutPosture.corroborating: The census independently records NO_GRADE_A_FULFILLMENT_RECORD for the three FL routes and AK, and launch-graph:operationallySellable=false / LAUNCH_GRAPH_CLOSED for HI, ME, both UT routes and WA.
checkoutPosture.oneThingTheCaptainShouldSeeAnyway: Every one of the nine compiled-profile routes carries paymentAuthority:'packet_checkout' and frontendBranch.paymentAllowed:true — including the five that are agency applications and not packets at all. That flag does NOT open checkout: packet-fulfillment-authority.ts names it explicitly among the proxies it refuses ('paymentAllowed copied from a profile is a stored opinion, and the thing that must be true is a present fact about an artifact'). So this is not a live exposure. It is a stored opinion that contradicts the route's own outcomeMode on five routes, and it will mislead the next reader who trusts it. Worth correcting at the profile level rather than per family.

hazardsForWhoeverPicksTheseUp.a3TrapWashington: WA-washington.json has no per-route filingDestinationRules or feeRules. It has PROFILE-LEVEL packetGenerator.filingDestinationRules, and every line in them addresses ADULT vacation under RCW 9.96.060 — CrRLJ 09.0100 / CR 08.0900, sentencing court, Certificate of Discharge, serve the prosecutor. That is a different statute and a different remedy from a 13.50.260 juvenile sealing motion. Under A3 it does NOT establish this route's filing destination. packetGenerator.feeRules is an empty array. This is the same shape as the California 1203.4 trap A3 was written for.
hazardsForWhoeverPicksTheseUp.a3TrapMaine: ME-maine.json packetGenerator.feeRules names a $60 post-judgment motion fee under Maine Rules of Civil Procedure 55(b)(2), 59, 60(b), 62 and 66 and tells the reader to confirm the exact CR-218/CR-289 fee with the clerk. CR-218 and CR-289 are the adult non-conviction and prostitution sealing instruments, not the § 3308-C juvenile petition. Under A3 that line does not answer this route's fee question. Separately, ME's packetGenerator.filingDestinationRules is not a filing destination at all — it is State Bureau of Identification records-ACCESS content ($31 online search, $41 notarized check). Do not publish either as this route's answer.
hazardsForWhoeverPicksTheseUp.destinationsAreEmpty: Census destination is 'not recorded' for ME, WA and UT path-L, and 'exact filing destination not recorded' for UT path-M. Whoever builds these will have to establish the court from the route contract or say honestly that no held source names it and name the office to ask, per A1 as widened by A2.
hazardsForWhoeverPicksTheseUp.pendingRouteKindAdjudications: ME juvenile-sealing, UT path-L and UT path-M each carry route-kind-adjudication:pending. The route contract says participant_packet; the evaluator evidence says 'not a user-filed court petition' (UT pair conclusive=true with prior=guidance_only; ME conclusive=false with prior=needs_more_info). The same census rows carry runtime-authority-decision effective-notes directing that the contradictory guidance-only treatment be removed where the statute expressly authorises a participant-filed petition, and the census resolves currentOutputStrategy to the petition. So the record points one way, but the adjudication is formally open and a Captain should close it before a packet lane finishes those three. WA carries no such pending adjudication.
